evidence: Receiving DO2 step change from 12.94 mg/L at 46.0 h to 8.50 mg/L at 46.2 h, continuing decline to 7.41 mg/L at 52.0 h
Source batches at 52 h: 10.88 (source-1), 10.81 (source-2), 11.47 (source-3) mg/L — receiving is 3+ mg/L below source envelope
Receiving P at 48 h = 3.025 g/L, matching source-1/2/3 at 48 h (3.057/3.017/2.979 g/L) — growth/product not yet compromised
DO2 remains above the 2 mg/L minimum constraint even at the 52 h minimum of 7.41 mg/L
No feed-related evidence of excess or limitation in available observations
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 abruptly fell at 46.2 h (12.9 → 8.2 mg/L) and has declined steadily to 7.4 mg/L by 52 h, while all three source batches at the same age still run ~10.5–11.5 mg/L. The product trajectory (P ≈ 3.03 g/L at 48 h, matching sources at ~3.0 g/L) shows production is on track, so the deviation is consistent with oxygen uptake demand outstripping transfer capacity in the receiving vessel, not a feed excess. increase_air raises the aeration factor within its bounded range (1.0 → 1.15), directly addressing the OTR shortfall without cutting feed and thus without sacrificing product mass, and keeps DO comfortably above the 2 mg/L minimum. Alternatives considered: KEEP risks continued DO decline and eventual oxygen-limited production; reduce_feed/combined/strong feed cuts reduce substrate and likely product mass without evidence of feed-related cause; stop yields zero counted production. No extra assay was requested: the online DO2 evidence is unambiguous and a 4 h assay delay would not change the oxygen-transfer diagnosis.
submission.uncertainty: The exact aeration headroom of the receiving vessel is unknown; if blower/OTR capacity is already near its limit, a 15% increase may only partially restore DO. Hidden receiving parameters may also include a different oxygen demand kinetics than sources, so the DO recovery magnitude is uncertain. Feed state is unobserved, so a covert feed excess cannot be fully excluded — if DO fails to recover post-intervention, feed reduction would be the next bounded step.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 12.94 mg/L at 46.0 h dropping to 8.50 mg/L at 46.2 h and declining to 7.41-7.89 mg/L by 50-52 h
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 0.998 g/L (36h sample, avail 40h) and 3.025 g/L (48h sample, avail 52h) showing active production
Source batches show analogous mid-run DO2 dips (~24-27h) that recover after feed/air changes, indicating feed-driven oxygen demand
physical_forward_model KEEP: min DO2 2.37 mg/L (sensitivity 2.16), product 315.5 kg - near oxygen-limit violation
physical_forward_model strong_feed_reduction: min DO2 5.71 mg/L (sensitivity 3.13-7.20), product 621.6 kg (sensitivity 616.6-627.4 kg), all members feasible
physical_forward_model comparisons: increase_air 357.3 kg (min DO 3.04), reduce_feed 598.1 kg (min DO 3.18), combined 597.3 kg (min DO 4.02)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 fell sharply at 46.2 h (12.9 to 8.5 mg/L) and is drifting down toward the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit while product accumulates; the KEEP baseline is predicted to come within 0.2-0.4 mg/L of the constraint and forfeits roughly half the achievable product mass. Strong feed reduction plus increased aeration maximizes predicted product mass (~622 kg vs 315 kg for KEEP) while providing the largest oxygen safety margin (predicted min DO2 5.7 mg/L, worst sensitivity member 3.1 mg/L), with all sensitivity members feasible. Bounded interventions (increase_air, reduce_feed, combined) improve on KEEP but are dominated by strong_feed_reduction on both mass and DO margin in the nominal model.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated (estimated transfer multiplier 0.66 from receiving observations) and may not match the hidden receiving realization; the 0.6 feed factor is aggressive and could over-restrict production if receiving kinetics differ, though all sensitivity members remain feasible with large DO margins. Sensor noise (~0.3 mg/L) and the possibility that the 46 h DO2 drop is a transient (as in source batches around 24 h that recover) mean KEEP could still be viable, but the downside risk of an oxygen violation and lost product mass outweighs that. No extra assay was requested since the decision at 52 h is already supported by online DO2 and delayed product data.
